Q26
Project Description #1 – Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
In 2022 the Bell CHC Marker Committee formed a partnership with the City of Temple, the Texas Historical Commission, the Texas
Ranger Hall of Fame, the Daughters of the Republic of Texas Belton and Temple Chapters, the property owners WB Development, and
the land acquisition managers DR Horton. Together we entered a collaborative agreement to preserve the historic battlefield of the
famed 1839 Texas Ranger engagement with Commanche, Caddo and Kickapoo natives. In 2023 the City was granted permission by
the THC to move a 1936 gray granite Texas Centennial historical marker, titled “Bird Creek Indian Battle,” from a TxDOT right of way
on Nugent Ave. to the actual battlefield near the ravine that the Rangers were pinned down. The Marker Committee and City prepared
an application for a Subject Marker for the Commanche Hunting Grounds Battle, which was approved in 2023 by the THC. The Marker
Committee and City have developed a preservation plan for interpretation that will tell the story of the battle from both sides of the
conflict using interpretive signage. WB Development and DR Horton have approved placement on the land and sectioned off the
battlefield site and in 2023 created a park-like setting with sidewalks and benches to view the battlefield, the ravine, and the relocated
marker, including siting the location of the future Subject Marker. The DRT has received approval for a historicc medallion to be
included at the centennial marker, and will provide signage at the entrance of the interpretive walkway. This project will provide another
major heritage tourism destination site in Bell County, the first of its kind. The project is ongoing and may take 18-24 months to
complete.

Q27
Project Description #2 – Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
The Bell County Historical Commission Grants sub committee recommended awarding four grants in 2022 totaling $6000. Each year,
the commission accepts grant applications September 1 through October 31 and considers any project, except construction, for
funding. Non-profit, tax-exempt organizations or institutions located in Bell County are eligible to apply. Grants recommended for
approval in 2023 for disbursement in 2024 were:
1. Salado Museum and College Park - $1000 to modernize display cases.
2. Bartlett Activity Center - $2800 for maintenance to their gravel roof of the old red brick activity center, originally the 1909 grammar
school, is the only remaining building by Austin architect A.O. Watson.
3. Dyess Family Cemetery - $ 1,000.00 for a headstone releveling project. The Dyess Family Cemetery Association will match
$1000.00 to complete this project.
4. Temple Public Library, Springer Archives Division - $1,200.00 for Bell County rail artifact digitization.
This project will allow for modernization and restoration of historic resources located within the county.

Q28
Project Description #3 – Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
In 2023 the Bell CHC embarked on long-term stewardship and survey project to develop a county map highlighting historical locations
to direct the public to prominent landmarks and sites of interest while encouraging heritage tourism across our county. The
Commission formed a subcommittee to plan this directory, to be completed in time for the 125th anniversary of Bell County in 2025.
The map will include a guide of select facilities, properties, landmarks, historic sites and items of interest that are open to the public,
with a location plotted on the paper map which can be distributed by partner agencies and organizations. The borders of the map will
tell the history of the county, including associated landmarks and items of interest. The project is ongoing and may take 18-24 months
to complete.
